MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.




About the Role



Oracle Fusion Application Analyst




Key support role - Oracle Fusion Cloud (ERP-SCM) environment


Provide functional and technical support for Monash Health's critical enterprise application.


Permanent, full time role, based at Scoresby Corporate Site




Monash Health is the largest healthcare provider in Victoria and is recognised for its exceptional clinical care and research. We are dedicated to providing outstanding patient care. We appreciate our unique and vital role as an integral part of the communities we serve and the importance of maintaining our services in a changing environment. The integrity of our corporate systems is critical to our ability to deliver excellent care to every patient, every time.



This role represents a great opportunity within our newly formed Applications and Enablement team. Reporting to the Manager Finance Systems, you'll be part of a team responsible for ensuring our systems perform reliably and consistently, delivering both business continuity and continuous improvement. Working closely with business stakeholders, vendors and in-house digital teams, you'll play an integral role in optimising Oracle Fusion to help Monash Health deliver tomorrow's care today.



If appointed, your contribution will be assessed across five Key Result Areas:




Operational Support


System Configuration and Maintenance


Stakeholder Engagement


Continuous Improvement


Governance, Risk and Compliance




This role is expected to work in a hybrid model, with a minimum of three days per week on site in our Scoresby Office.




About you


The Oracle Application Analyst ensures the effective integration of technology with all business functions to maximize organisational performance. Develops and maintains positive relationships between Business Services and its customers. With strong system knowledge and highly developed communication skills you can demonstrate the ability to translate technical problems into language that's easy to understand for non-technical stakeholders. 



Naturally curious, you readily analyse business processes and translate requirements into system solutions. Above all, you are a committed team player who enjoys working collaboratively with colleagues to provide a consistently high level of service to your stakeholders. 



On a personal level, you are:




Highly organised


Flexible and able to adapt readily to changing priorities 


A highly effective communicator, with active listening skills


Sound technical understanding of systems and related business processes




What you need



To be considered for this role, you will need to demonstrate:




Tertiary qualification in Information Technology or Business 


Strong functional knowledge of one or more Oracle Fusion modules (ERP, EPM, SCM)


Experience working within an Application Managed Services (AMS) or shared services support model


Proven ability to analyse incidents, identify root causes and coordinate resolution across a number of teams


Demonstrated experience providing Level 2 and Level 3 application support for Oracle Fusion Could, in a complex enterprise environment


Experience with incident, problem and change management in an enterprise environment




While not mandatory requirements, experience with the following will be highly regarded:




Supporting integrations, reporting and security roles within Oracle Fusion


Oracle Fusion reporting tools (OTBI and BI Publisher) 


Familiarity with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) and enterprise integrations




We are especially interested in hearing from you if you've worked in a large public sector or healthcare organisation. 




Benefits of working at Monash Health




Monash Health offers a range of benefits, including: 




Comprehensive employee health and wellbeing programs including Fitness Passport


Five weeks annual leave with leave loading


Monthly ADOs for full-time employees 


Salary packaging benefits



For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Sherree O'Connell, Head of Enterprise Corporate Applications and Enablement on 0451 309 776


Position Description can be found here





Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 







Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 







You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 







We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 







We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. 





How to Apply


Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system. For information including how to apply and probity check requirements, please click here for the 'Application Guide'


Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date.

## Cyber Security Operations Coordinator
## Position Overview
We are looking for a skilled and proactive Cyber Security Operations Coordinator to lead the coordination and response to complex cyber security incidents, threat hunting investigations, and cross-functional security operations. This role plays a critical part in safeguarding organisational systems and data by driving incident response activities, advising leadership on operational matters, and contributing to strategic security planning. The ideal candidate is a technically proficient security professional with strong coordination capabilities, sound analytical judgement, and the ability to communicate complex security issues clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
## Key Responsibilities
- Lead the end-to-end investigation and response to cyber security incidents, including containment, mitigation, and recovery activities, ensuring timely resolution and minimal operational disruption
- Direct threat hunting operations to proactively identify threat vectors, develop threat models, and build security cases that inform defensive strategies across the organisation
- Analyse security risks, vulnerabilities, and emerging threats, translating findings into actionable security plans and technical controls aligned with the organisation's security architecture
- Coordinate and manage tasks across multiple teams during incident response and threat hunt engagements, ensuring clear communication, accountability, and effective workflow throughout each operation
- Advise senior leadership on the status of current security operations, ongoing collaborations, and key findings, contributing meaningfully to strategic security planning and policy development
- Develop and communicate key messaging around security incidents and threat intelligence, ensuring accurate and timely information is delivered to the appropriate stakeholders
- Oversee the collection, preservation, and forensic analysis of digital evidence in accordance with established procedures and chain-of-custody requirements
- Implement and maintain technical security controls that align with the organisation's security strategies, frameworks, and compliance obligations
- Perform ongoing threat management activities, monitoring threat landscapes and updating security models to reflect evolving attack techniques and adversary behaviours
- Facilitate and coordinate security awareness training programmes for staff, promoting a security-conscious culture across the organisation
- Maintain detailed records of incident response activities, investigation findings, and operational outcomes to support continuous improvement and audit readiness
- Collaborate with internal teams and external partners to uphold the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of organisational systems and information assets
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- Bachelor's degree in Cyber Security, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience
- Demonstrated experience in a cyber security operations, incident response, or threat intelligence role, with exposure to coordinating cross-functional teams
- Strong working knowledge of incident response methodologies, threat hunting techniques, and digital forensics processes
- Experience conducting security risk assessments, vulnerability analyses, and developing actionable remediation plans
- Proficiency with security tools and platforms such as SIEM, EDR, IDS/IPS, and threat intelligence feeds
- Solid understanding of security frameworks and standards, including NIST, ISO 27001, or the Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) Essential Eight
- Demonstrated ability to analyse and interpret complex technical information and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
- Strong project coordination and task management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities in a high-pressure environment
- Sound understanding of network security, endpoint protection, identity and access management, and cloud security principles
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience producing professional reports, briefings, and incident documentation
## Preferred Qualifications
- Industry certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CEH, GIAC (e.g. GCIH, GCFA), or CompTIA Security+
- Experience working within a Security Operations Centre (SOC) environment or managed security services setting
- Familiarity with Australian regulatory and compliance requirements, including the Privacy Act, Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, and relevant sector-specific obligations
- Exposure to threat intelligence platforms, malware analysis, or reverse engineering
- Experience contributing to the development of security policies, procedures, or organisational security awareness programmes
- Prior experience briefing or advising senior leadership or executive stakeholders on cyber security matters
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a collaborative and forward-thinking security team where your contributions directly shape the organisation's cyber resilience
- Access ongoing professional development opportunities, including support for industry certifications, training programmes, and conference attendance
- Enjoy a flexible working environment that supports work-life balance, including hybrid work arrangements
- Competitive remuneration package with superannuation, reflective of your skills and experience
- Work within a values-driven organisation committed to innovation, integrity, and building a diverse and inclusive workplace
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Superannuation

Our firm works closely with business and individual clients to thoughtfully manage financial affairs, effectively manage risks, identify opportunities and support long-term growth.

This role involves responsibility for managing a diverse portfolio of clients and delivering a range of high-quality accounting, taxation and advisory services. The successful candidate will contribute to client success by ensuring accurate compliance work as well as being an asset within the firm’s collaborative environment.

Key Responsibilities

- Preparation of financial statements and income tax returns for a variety of entities including individuals, companies, trusts and partnerships

- Ongoing client liaison and advisory support
- Use of cloud accounting software to manage, reconcile and analyse accounts

Essential Skills & Experience

- conducting financial investigations, preparing reports, undertaking audits and advising on matters such as the purchase and sale of businesses, mergers, capital financing, suspected fraud, insolvency and taxation
